dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Washington Hosts Bengals on Monday Night Football Amid Defensive Struggles
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Washington (3-5-1) enters Monday's matchup against the 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals as significant underdogs, facing the NFL's top-ranked passing offense with a secondary ranked #31 in yards allowed. While the Commanders' 13.8% playoff probability remains slim, the team relies on a +7 turnover differential and the return of a healthy Jayden Daniels to spark an upset.
bullets: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is expected to be at full strength after participating fully in practice, presenting a major test for a Washington defense allowing a #30 ranked 71.9% touchdown rate in the red zone [S7](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50544261/burrow-practices-again-full-strength-mnf).

Defensive Coordinator Daronte Jones must find ways to pressure Burrow despite a #25 ranked sack rate, as Cincinnati leads the league in passing EPA and third-down conversion efficiency [S3](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49828234/washington-commanders-daronte-jones-2026-defense).

The Commanders will wear their new 'Hail Raiser' uniforms at Northwest Stadium, where the organization hopes a raucous environment can mitigate Cincinnati's statistical advantages in special teams and punting [S6](https://www.commanders.com/news/raucous-hail-raiser-fan-environment-can-make-big-difference-against-bengals) [S9](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50514892/nfl-week-11-uniforms).

Personnel availability is mixed; while Jayden Daniels and key offensive linemen are cleared, Washington remains without Pro Bowlers Terry McLaurin and Daron Payne, who are both on Injured Reserve [S10](https://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/50543810/commanders-confident-jayden-daniels).
